body.title: Saurashtrian Migrants and Vaigai Silt: The Sungudi Knot-and-Dye Handloom Heritage
body.orientation: How skilled migrant weavers from Gujarat settled in Madurai, fusing tie-and-dye techniques with South Indian temple cotton borders.

hero.alt: Artisan tying thousands of tiny knots on Madurai Sungudi cotton fabric before dyeing

paragraphs.text: During the 16th century, master weavers from Saurashtra migrated south to escape political upheavals, receiving asylum and royal patronage from the Nayak rulers of Madurai.
In Madurai, they developed Sungudi (from the Sanskrit 'Sunnam', meaning round spot): fine combed cotton fabric patterned by tying thousands of tiny knots by hand using fingernails and thread.

sections.heading: Natural dyes and the Vaigai River

paragraphs.text: The cloth was traditionally washed and treated in the mineral-rich waters of the Vaigai River, which bonded the natural madder red and indigo dyes permanently to the cotton fibers.
Sungudi represents a magnificent synthesis of Western Indian Bandhani tie-dye with Tamil temple borders (zari karai), awarded Geographical Indication protection.

followUpQuestions: How do Saurashtrian Tamils maintain their unique language and culinary traditions in Madurai?
What distinguishes authentic Sungudi knot-dyeing from screen-printed imitations?

claims.text: Saurashtrian weavers migrated to Madurai under Nayak patronage in the 16th and 17th centuries.

evidence.excerpt: The craft was brought to Madurai by Saurashtrian weavers who migrated to the Tamil region upon invitation by King Thirumalai Nayak.

claims.text: Sungudi textiles are characterized by minute hand-tied knots producing circular dot patterns.

evidence.excerpt: The fabric is pinch-tied with thread thousands of times by hand before being immersed in dye baths.

claims.text: Washing the tied cotton in the Vaigai River water helped fix natural mineral dyes.

evidence.excerpt: The waters of the Vaigai River were traditionally used to rinse and fix the dyes onto the combed cotton yarn.

claims.text: Madurai Sungudi possesses Geographical Indication (GI) status under Indian law.

evidence.excerpt: Madurai Sungudi has been registered under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act.
